mcat_description.short: Portable classrooms are prefabricated, modular cabin-style structures designed for use as temporary or semi-permanent educational spaces, typically built with steel frames and insulated PUF or sandwich panels and assembled on-site from factory-manufactured components.
mcat_description.long: Portable classrooms are factory-built, modular structures used as functional learning spaces by schools, coaching institutes, NGOs, and government education programs requiring rapid infrastructure deployment. They are constructed using steel or light gauge steel frames (LGSF) clad with insulated sandwich panels — PUF (polyurethane foam), EPS, or cement board — providing thermal insulation, structural durability, and weather resistance across India's diverse climatic zones. Sold as turnkey units or custom-dimensioned structures, they can be single-room cabins or multi-module school buildings with electrical, plumbing, and HVAC provisions, and are fully relocatable when educational needs change. Key advantages over traditional construction include significantly reduced build time (weeks vs. months), lower labour costs, and the ability to expand or relocate the structure as institutional requirements evolve.

market_context: In the Indian market, portable classrooms are predominantly manufactured as steel-framed prefabricated cabin structures clad with PUF (polyurethane foam) or EPS insulated sandwich panels, providing thermal comfort across India's varied climates. Leading Indian manufacturers include EPACK Prefab, Pressmach, Hayajami Porta Solutions, Suchintan Enterprises, and Tata Steel Nest-In (MobiNest product line), with manufacturing hubs concentrated in Delhi-NCR, Mumbai/Thane, Ahmedabad, and Bengaluru. Two dominant structural technologies are observed: (1) conventional mild steel frame with PUF/EPS sandwich panels — the volume segment; and (2) LGSF (Light Gauge Steel Framing) with insulated panels — a premium, seismically-rated variant gaining traction for government and institutional projects. Cladding options include PPGL, GI sheet, cement board, and ACP panels. Buyers typically specify floor area (commonly 10×10 ft to larger multi-room configurations), insulation type, cladding material, and whether electrical/plumbing/HVAC provisions are required. The category sits within the broader Portable Cabin taxonomy on IndiaMART, with sibling categories including Prefabricated School Building (for permanent multi-storey structures) and Portable Buildings. Demand is driven by school expansion needs, government rural education programs, NGO-run learning centres, and coaching institutes — with disaster-relief and emergency education deployment as a secondary use case.
